{{short description|American ethnomathematician}}
[[File:Tinne Hoff Kjeldsen and Marcia Ascher, Oberwolfach Photo Collection.jpg|thumb|]]
'''Marcia Alper Ascher''' (April 23, 1935 – August 10, 2013) was an American mathematician, and a leader and pioneer in [[ethnomathematics]].{{r|pass}} She was a [[professor emerita]] of mathematics at [[Ithaca College]].{{r|enc|obit}}

==Life==
Ascher was born in [[New York City]], the daughter of a glazier and a secretary. She graduated from [[Queens College, City University of New York]] in 1956,{{r|enc}} and married [[Robert Ascher]], an anthropologist graduating from Queens College in the same year.{{r|enc|robert}}

They both became graduate students at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]];{{r|robert}} she completed a master's degree in 1960,{{r|enc}} and moved with her husband to [[Ithaca, New York]], where he had found a faculty position at [[Cornell University]].{{r|robert}}

She joined the mathematics department at Ithaca College in 1960, as one of the founders of the department.{{r|pass|obit}} She retired as full professor emerita in 1995.{{r|pass|enc}}

She died on August 10, 2013.{{r|maa|obit}}

==Books==
With her husband, Ascher co-authored the book ''[[Code of the Quipu|Code of the Quipu: A Study in Media, Mathematics, and Culture]]'' (University of Michigan Press, 1981); it was republished in 1997 by Dover Books as ''Mathematics of the Incas: Code of the Quipu''.{{r|code}} She was also the sole author of two more books on ethnomathematics, ''Ethnomathematics: A Multicultural View of Mathematical Ideas'' (Brooks/Cole, 1991){{r|ethno}} and ''Mathematics Elsewhere: An Exploration of Ideas across Cultures'' (Princeton University Press, 2002).{{r|elsewhere}} The Basic Library List Committee of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] has recommended the inclusion of all three books in undergraduate mathematics libraries.{{r|bll}} ''Mathematics Elsewhere'' won an honorable mention in the 2002 [[PROSE Awards]] in the mathematics and statistics category.{{r|prose}}
